destinations.name: Bengaluru
destinations.description: India's garden city and tech capital, known for cafés, breweries, markets and a cosmopolitan food scene.
destinations.season_note: October–February is most comfortable; visitable year-round.
destinations.entry_fee_note: City destination; no single confirmed main-attraction fee. Individual sites charge separately.
destinations.local_dish: Crispy Benne Masala Dosa and filter coffee at Vidyarthi Bhavan or CTR; Bisi Bele Bath and Akki Rotti with coconut chutney.
destinations.best_time_tip: Best visited October to February; explore Lalbagh Botanical Garden before 8:00 AM for tranquil walks and morning birdwatching.
destinations.practical_tip: Use the Namma Metro (Purple & Green lines) to bypass road traffic between central sights; avoid Silk Board and MG Road during peak 5:30–8:00 PM.

destinations.name: Mysuru
destinations.description: The cultural capital of Karnataka, famous for its illuminated palace, Dasara festivities and traditional markets.
destinations.season_note: Year-round; October–March is the most comfortable sightseeing window.
destinations.entry_fee_note: City destination; Mysore Palace and other site fees were not verified in this data pass.
destinations.local_dish: Original Mylari butter masala dosa at Hotel Original Vinayaka Mylari; warm Mysore Pak from Guru Sweet Mart; traditional plantain-leaf South Karnataka thali.
destinations.best_time_tip: Tour Mysore Palace interior around 10:00 AM in natural daylight; witness the grand 100,000-bulb evening palace illumination on Sundays and public holidays (7:00–7:45 PM).
destinations.practical_tip: Ascend Chamundi Hill before 7:30 AM to beat pilgrimage crowds; pre-book audio guides at the palace south gate.

destinations.name: Srirangapatna
destinations.description: Island fortress town of Tipu Sultan on the Cauvery, with temples, tombs and gardens close to Mysuru.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Monument fees (e.g. Dariya Daulat) not confirmed as current.
destinations.local_dish: Fresh Kaveri river fish fry or Mandya-style Ragi Mudde with Bassaru, accompanied by fresh tender coconut water along the riverbanks.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit between September and March; explore Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace (Dariya Daulat Bagh) in the morning when the teakwood frescoes are best illuminated.
destinations.practical_tip: Hire a certified local ASI guide outside the fort gate for 45 minutes to appreciate Tipu Sultan's rocket launching posts and historic river battle breach points.

destinations.name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
destinations.description: Riverine sanctuary on the Cauvery with nesting islands, crocodiles and boat rides — a short detour from Mysuru.
destinations.season_note: December–February for migratory birds; June–November for the nesting season.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Sanctuary entry ₹80 per Indian adult (ticketing site).
destinations.local_dish: Packed riverside breakfast with hot Maddur Vada, tender coconut water, and traditional South Indian filter coffee in nearby Srirangapatna.
destinations.best_time_tip: Peak migratory bird nesting season runs December to April; early morning 8:30 AM boat rides offer calm river currents and optimal bird photography.
destinations.practical_tip: Opt for the guided forest department rowboat tour with lifejackets; maintain strict silence near the islet nesting trees and crocodile basking rocks.

destinations.name: Melkote
destinations.description: Temple town on a granite hill above the Cauvery plains, known for Cheluvanarayana Swamy and its step tank.
destinations.entry_fee_note: No main-attraction fee confirmed.
destinations.local_dish: Iconic Melkote Puliyogare (tangy tamarind rice spiced with sesame and groundnuts) and sweet Sakkare Pongal from Subbanna Mess.
destinations.best_time_tip: Climb the 300 rock-cut steps to Yoga Narasimha Temple at sunrise (6:30 AM) to catch the morning breeze and sweeping 360-degree views across the Mandya plains.
destinations.practical_tip: Purchase genuine GI-tagged Melkote handloom cotton dhotis and sarees directly from the local weavers' cooperative society.

destinations.name: Bannerghatta Biological Park
destinations.description: National park and biological park on Bengaluru's southern edge with safari, zoo and butterfly park.
destinations.season_note: October–February for comfortable weather; wildlife sightings can be strong March–May.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Non-AC bus safari incl. zoo: ₹370 weekdays / ₹420 weekends and holidays (official tariff effective 2025-08-01).
destinations.local_dish: South Indian thali, hot masala vada, and refreshing spiced buttermilk available at the forest department eco-canteen.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit between October and March on weekdays; arrive by 9:00 AM when ticket counters open to secure first-slot AC safari tickets.
destinations.practical_tip: Pre-book the Grand Safari combo online to skip the main queue; the 2-hour morning safari offers the highest chance of spotting royal Bengal tigers and lions active.

destinations.name: Hampi
destinations.description: A UNESCO World Heritage site of boulder-strewn landscapes and the ruined splendour of the Vijayanagara Empire.
destinations.entry_fee_note: ASI monument entry ₹40 for Indian adults (ASI/Wikipedia).
destinations.accessibility_notes: Monument zone is spread over rocky, uneven terrain with boulders and slopes.
destinations.local_dish: Authentic North Karnataka Jolada Rotti meals with Yennegai (spiced stuffed baby brinjal), Shenga peanut chutney, and Mango Tree's special thali.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit November to February; climb Matanga Hill at 5:45 AM for sunrise over the boulder landscape, and watch sunset from Hemakuta Hill.
destinations.practical_tip: Rent a bicycle or moped to navigate the 26 sq km complex; temple sanctums require removing footwear, so wear slip-on walking shoes with socks.

destinations.name: Badami
destinations.description: Rock-cut cave temples of the Chalukyas set above a red sandstone lake, gateway to the Aihole–Pattadakal circuit.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.accessibility_notes: Cave temples are reached by climbing rock-cut steps.
destinations.local_dish: Traditional Bagalkot Jolada Rotti thali with Yennegai badane, spicy Shenga Hindi (flaxseed/peanut powder), and fresh thick buffalo curd.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit Cave Temples at 7:00 AM when the morning golden hour illuminates the sandstone rock-cut carvings across Cave 1 to Cave 4.
destinations.practical_tip: Walk the scenic circuit around Agastya Lake to Bhootnath Temples before 9:30 AM; watch out for inquisitive monkeys along the canyon cliff steps.

destinations.name: Aihole
destinations.description: Open-air museum of early Chalukyan temples and rock-cut shrines on the Malaprabha river.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Hot Bagalkot-style Jowar rotti with roasted gram chutney, sprouts usli, and freshly churned country butter.
destinations.best_time_tip: Best visited October to March; explore the Durga Temple and its unique apsidal colonnade during quiet morning hours (8:00–10:30 AM).
destinations.practical_tip: Begin at the ASI Archaeological Museum next to Durga Temple for site context on the 120+ 5th-to-8th-century Chalukyan experimental temples.

destinations.name: Pattadakal
destinations.description: UNESCO-listed cluster of Chalukyan temples blending northern and southern Indian temple styles.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: North Karnataka rural vegetarian oota with Jolada rotti, Pithla (gram flour curry), and fresh curd.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit in late afternoon (3:30–5:30 PM) when warm slanting sunlight reveals the exquisite details of the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temple friezes.
destinations.practical_tip: Carry an umbrella and water bottle as there is minimal tree canopy between monuments across this UNESCO World Heritage complex.

destinations.name: Vijayapura
destinations.description: Adilshahi capital with the monumental Gol Gumbaz, imperial mosques and fine Indo-Islamic architecture.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Gol Gumbaz Indian adult ticket ₹20 (ticketing source).
destinations.local_dish: Authentic Vijayapura Jolada Rotti with spicy Shenga chutney, spiced brinjal curry, and historic local sweet Gulgule.
destinations.best_time_tip: Enter Gol Gumbaz right at 8:30 AM; ascend to the Whispering Gallery before crowds arrive to clearly hear the remarkable 11-time acoustic echo.
destinations.practical_tip: Hire a licensed guide at Ibrahim Rauza ('The Black Taj') to explore the delicate minarets and subterranean chambers.

destinations.name: Bidar
destinations.description: The northernmost fortress of the Deccan, with a majestic fort, Bahmani monuments and handmade paper craft.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Bidar Biryani, spicy Kalyana Karnataka Jolada Rotti with chana masala, and traditional sweet Shahi Tukda.
destinations.best_time_tip: Best visited October to February; explore the extensive Bidar Fort ramparts and Rangeen Mahal's mother-of-pearl inlay tiles in the morning.
destinations.practical_tip: Visit the local craft workshops near the fort to buy authentic GI-tagged Bidriware (blackened zinc and copper alloy inlaid with pure silver wire).

destinations.name: Kalaburagi
destinations.description: Former Bahmani capital with the spectacular Jama Masjid, mystic dargahs and rich Sufi heritage.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Kalaburagi Malpuri sweet, fiery Jolada Rotti meals with Gongura (sorrel leaf) chutney, and hot spicy Dalcha.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit during the cool winter months (November to February); tour the 14th-century Jami Masjid inside Gulbarga Fort in the morning.
destinations.practical_tip: When visiting the Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah, dress conservatively covering head and shoulders, and remove footwear at the outer gateway.

destinations.name: Belagavi
destinations.description: A fort city of Kittur Rani Chennamma with colonial-era libraries, temples and a pleasant plateau climate.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Famous Belagavi Kunda (slow-simmered caramelized milk sweet), hot Mandige (paper-thin sugar crêpe), and North Karnataka Jolada Rotti with spiced curries.
destinations.best_time_tip: Best visited September to February; visit Gokak Falls and Belagavi Fort ramparts between October and December when water volume is high and air is cool.
destinations.practical_tip: Visit the 13th-century Kamal Basti (Jain temple) inside Belagavi Fort in the early morning; stop at Camp area sweet shops for fresh hot Kunda.

destinations.name: Shravanabelagola
destinations.description: Ancient Jain pilgrimage town crowned by the colossal Gommateshwara Bahubali statue.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.accessibility_notes: The Gommateshwara statue on Vindhyagiri is reached by climbing roughly 400+ stone steps; Chandragiri hill is easier.
destinations.local_dish: Traditional Jain and satvik Karnataka oota: mild rasam, steamed rice, bean palya, and rich badam payasam.
destinations.best_time_tip: Start climbing the 620 granite steps up Vindhyagiri Hill before 8:00 AM; the bare stone rocks heat up significantly under midday sun.
destinations.practical_tip: Carry an extra pair of thick cotton socks to walk comfortably on the sunny temple stone courtyard around the 57-foot monolithic Bahubali statue.

destinations.name: Belur
destinations.description: Hoysala-era temple town on the Yagachi river, home to the intricately carved Chennakeshava Temple.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Hassan-style Akki Rotti with fresh coconut chutney, Obbattu (sweet lentil flatbread), and hot filter coffee.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit Chennakeshava Temple between 8:00 AM and 11:00 AM; morning light from the east illuminates the intricate soapstone facade.
destinations.practical_tip: Look closely under the temple eaves for the 42 Madanika (bracket dancer) figures; each depicts an intricate classical pose, hairstyle, and costume.

destinations.name: Halebidu
destinations.description: Former Hoysala capital with the monumental Hoysaleswara Temple set beside a lake.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Traditional Hoysala vegetarian lunch: hot rice, fragrant saaru, kootu, and crispy sandige (sun-dried crisps).
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit in late afternoon (3:00–5:30 PM) when the setting sun highlights the 30,000 detailed soapstone animal and mythological friezes.
destinations.practical_tip: Walk the complete exterior star-shaped base of Hoysaleshwara Temple clockwise to follow the continuous narrative relief of the Mahabharata and Ramayana.

destinations.name: Somanathapura
destinations.description: Small Cauvery-bank village with a perfectly preserved trikuta Chennakeshava temple.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Available fee reference only reports a 2020 price; not treated as current.
destinations.local_dish: Mysore region rural plantain-leaf meals: hot Bisi Bele Bath with boondi, spiced buttermilk, and Obbattu.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit mid-morning (9:30–11:30 AM); the trikuta (triple-sanctum) Keshava Temple has remarkable intact ceiling carvings best seen in morning light.
destinations.practical_tip: Hire an ASI-registered monument guide for 30 minutes; the 16 ceiling canopies each feature completely distinct blooming lotus and plantain flower carvings.

destinations.name: Hubballi
destinations.description: Twin commercial cities with a lively street-food culture, centuries-old temples and easy access to Dandeli.
destinations.entry_fee_note: City destination; no single confirmed main-attraction fee.
destinations.local_dish: Hubli-Dharwad famous Dharwad Peda (rich caramelized milk fudge from Babu Singh's Thakur Peda) and crispy Girmit (puffed rice snack) with Mirchi Bajji.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit October to March; enjoy the sunset breeze and boating at Unkal Lake around 5:00 PM.
destinations.practical_tip: Visit the ancient 12th-century Western Chalukyan Chandramouleshwara Temple near Unkal early in the morning before city traffic builds up.

destinations.name: Dandeli
destinations.description: Jungle adventure hub on the Kali River offering rafting, kayaking, coracle rides and hornbill spotting.
destinations.season_note: Rafting season depends on river flow; confirm locally before booking.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Rafting/activity prices are operator-dependent and were not confirmed in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: North Canara Malnad meals: hot Jolada Rotti with bamboo shoot curry, spicy green chutney, and refreshing herbal Kokum saru.
destinations.best_time_tip: White-water rafting season on the Kali River is best from October to May; dam water releases usually occur between 9:00 AM and 1:00 PM.
destinations.practical_tip: Pre-book Kali river rafting and forest jungle safaris with certified operators; wear quick-dry clothing and carry waterproof cases for phones.

destinations.name: Gokarna
destinations.description: Temple town on the Arabian Sea with laid-back coves like Om Beach and Kudle Beach.
destinations.season_note: October–March; sea can be rough during the monsoon.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Mahabaleshwar Temple entry is free (per Wikipedia/Karnataka Tourism).
destinations.accessibility_notes: Beaches are reached via steps and short hill paths.
destinations.local_dish: Fresh Karavali seafood curry or Neer Dosa with vegetable gassi at Namaste Cafe on Om Beach; chilled Kokum sherbet and local cashew sweets.
destinations.best_time_tip: Best visited October to March; do the 4-km cliff trail hike across Kudle, Om, Half Moon, and Paradise beaches during morning low tide.
destinations.practical_tip: Carry cash as beach shacks frequently have erratic digital network connections; swim only in designated flags-marked zones.

destinations.name: Murudeshwar
destinations.description: Coastal shrine with a towering Shiva statue, gopura and island-fort views over the Arabian Sea.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Fresh coastal Karavali meals with red rice, fish fry / crisp raw banana podi, and local Sol Kadi.
destinations.best_time_tip: Take the 18-storey elevator inside the Raja Gopura at 9:00 AM for a 360-degree aerial panorama of the 123-foot Shiva statue and Arabian Sea.
destinations.practical_tip: Netrani Island scuba diving trips depart early morning (7:30 AM) from the harbor; confirm weather and sea conditions the day prior.

destinations.name: Yana
destinations.description: Limestone cave formations in the Sahyadri forests of Uttara Kannada, reached by a short forest walk.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Karnataka Tourism lists an approximate forest fee of ₹20–50; budget uses the ₹50 upper bound.
destinations.accessibility_notes: Reached on foot via a forest trail; involves walking on uneven ground.
destinations.local_dish: Kumta coastal Karavali thali with Neer Dosa, sweet banana halwa, and refreshing tender coconut water at the base trail.
destinations.best_time_tip: Hike the shaded forest path to the limestone monoliths (Bhairaveshwara and Mohini peaks) between 8:00 AM and 11:00 AM before afternoon humidity rises.
destinations.practical_tip: Wear trekking shoes with good grip as the limestone cave trail has damp patches; take a torch to explore the natural cave passage behind the rock.

destinations.name: Karwar
destinations.description: A quiet harbour town of Rabindranath Tagore fame with island-dotted bays and the Kali river estuary.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Authentic Karwar seafood thali with Surmai fry, red rice, and tangy Kokum kadhi; local jackfruit pappad and cashew sweets.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit between October and March; catch the panoramic sunset over the Kali River estuary from Sadashivgad Fort.
destinations.practical_tip: Take a 15-minute speed boat to Kurumgad Island or Devbagh Beach early morning for dolphin-spotting excursions.

destinations.name: Udupi & Manipal
destinations.description: Pilgrim town famous for the Krishna temple, student-town Manipal and the iconic Udupi dosa.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: World-famous satvik Udupi Brahmin oota on banana leaf at Mitra Samaj; hot Goli Baje, Neer Dosa, and authentic filter coffee near Car Street.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit Sri Krishna Matha during morning Nirmalya darshan (5:30–7:00 AM) or evening Mahapooja (7:00 PM) to experience the brass lamps and temple chariot.
destinations.practical_tip: Dress code at Sri Krishna Matha requires men to remove shirts and women to dress modestly (salwar/saree); take the 15-minute ferry from Malpe beach to St. Mary's columnar basalt islands.

destinations.name: Karkala
destinations.description: Coastal hinterland town known for its towering Gommateshwara statue and Jain heritage.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Gommateshwara statue has no entry fee (per sources cited).
destinations.local_dish: South Canara vegetarian delicacies: Jackfruit Gatti (steamed dumplings), Golibaje, Pathrode, and tender cashew nut curry.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit the 42-foot single-stone Gommateshwara statue atop the rocky hillock at sunset for cool breezes and sweeping Western Ghats views.
destinations.practical_tip: Combine the Gommateshwara hill with the 15th-century Chaturmukha Basadi, which has four identical stone entrances aligned with the cardinal directions.

destinations.name: Moodabidri
destinations.description: Jain temple town famous for the thousand-pillar Saavira Kambada Basadi.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Authentic Jain and Tuluva breakfast: Neer Dosa with coconut jaggery mixture, spicy uppittu, and fresh filter coffee.
destinations.best_time_tip: Explore the 15th-century Tribhuvana Tilaka Chudamani (Thousand Pillar Temple) in the morning; soft natural light illuminates the 1,000 unique granite carved pillars.
destinations.practical_tip: Notice that no two pillars in the entire Thousand Pillar Temple have identical carvings; inspect the outer granite base for dragons and giraffes depicting ancient maritime trade.

destinations.name: Mangaluru
destinations.description: Coastal port city with temple architecture, golden beaches and celebrated Mangalorean seafood.
destinations.entry_fee_note: City destination; no single confirmed main-attraction fee.
destinations.local_dish: Iconic Mangalorean cuisine: Neer Dosa with Kori Gassi (chicken curry) or vegetable stew, crispy Mangalore Buns, and rich Ghee Roast.
destinations.best_time_tip: Best visited October to February; visit Kudroli Gokarnath Temple in the evening when illuminated by thousands of golden lights.
destinations.practical_tip: Head to Panambur Beach in the late afternoon for water scooter rides and panoramic coastal sunsets; try Ideal Ice Cream's famous 'Gadbad' sundae.

destinations.name: Agumbe
destinations.description: Rainforest plateau in the Western Ghats famous for sunset points, king cobras and monsoon streams.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.accessibility_notes: Forest trails and waterfall walks involve uneven terrain.
destinations.local_dish: Malnad forest culinary specials: Halasina Hannina Happala (jackfruit pappad), steaming Kashaya herbal drink, and cooling Thambli.
destinations.best_time_tip: Known as the 'Cherrapunji of the South'; visit Sunset Point overlooking the Western Ghats canopy at 5:30 PM on clear winter evenings.
destinations.practical_tip: Apply natural insect repellent and wear leech socks when walking the rainforest trails to Barkana and Onake Abbi waterfalls.

destinations.name: Chikkamagaluru
destinations.description: Coffee-country hill district of misty peaks, waterfalls and plantation homestays.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Malnad specialties: Akki Rotti with Kaayi chutney, steaming Pathrode (colocasia roll), and freshly roasted Arabica estate filter coffee.
destinations.best_time_tip: Drive up Mullayanagiri peak (Karnataka's highest point at 1,930 m) before 8:00 AM; after 9:30 AM narrow mountain passes suffer vehicle congestion and heavy mist.
destinations.practical_tip: Book an estate tour at a local coffee plantation to observe harvesting, pulping, and bean roasting; carry a light jacket year-round.

destinations.name: Kudremukh
destinations.description: Rolling shola grasslands and the classic Kudremukh ridge trek in the Western Ghats.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Trek permit conditions/fees change seasonally; not confirmed in this pass.
destinations.accessibility_notes: Peak trek involves sustained uphill hiking.
destinations.local_dish: Nutritious Malnad trekking meals: hot ganji (rice porridge) with tender mango pickle, neer dosa, and fresh black pepper tea.
destinations.best_time_tip: Trekking season is October to February; obtain the mandatory forest department trek permit online in advance (strictly capped daily entries).
destinations.practical_tip: Start the 20-km horse-face peak trek by 6:00 AM from the base camp; carry your own water bottle as disposable plastic is strictly prohibited inside the National Park.

destinations.name: Sringeri
destinations.description: Sharada Peetham maths on the Tunga river, a major Advaita pilgrimage centre in the Ghats.
destinations.entry_fee_note: No entry fee confirmed for the maths.
destinations.local_dish: Sacred temple Annadana lunch served at the matha dining hall: satvik rice, sambar, rasam, and sweet payasam.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit Vidyashankara Temple at sunrise (6:30 AM); its 12 zodiac stone pillars are aligned so that the morning sun rays fall on the pillar corresponding to the current solar month.
destinations.practical_tip: Dress modestly covering shoulders and knees; feed puffed rice to the sacred mahseer fish in the Tunga river ghat steps outside the temple.

destinations.name: Shivamogga
destinations.description: Gateway city to Malnad, base for Jog Falls and wildlife sanctuaries with easy rail and air links.
destinations.entry_fee_note: City destination; no single confirmed main-attraction fee.
destinations.local_dish: Mid-Karnataka classics: Davangere Benne Dosa, spicy Mandakki Oggarane (seasoned puffed rice), and fresh Malnad filter coffee.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit between September and February; visit the Sakrebyle Elephant Camp at 8:30 AM to watch mahouts bathe elephants in the Tunga river backwaters.
destinations.practical_tip: Pre-book the lion and tiger safari at Tyavarekoppa; combining Sakrebyle in the morning and Tyavarekoppa in the afternoon makes an ideal wildlife day.

destinations.name: Jog Falls
destinations.description: One of India's highest plunge waterfalls, a four-cascade drop in the Sharavathi valley.
highlights: Viewing platforms for Raja, Rani, Rocket & Roarer
destinations.season_note: Peak flow during and just after the monsoon (August–December).
destinations.entry_fee_note: Viewpoint entry ₹20 for Indian adults (per Karnataka Tourism reference).
destinations.accessibility_notes: Viewpoints involve walking; the falls edge has railings.
destinations.local_dish: Simple Sahyadri hill-station canteen meals: hot Mirchi Bajji with ginger tea, lemon rice, and curd rice overlooking the gorge.
destinations.best_time_tip: Peak water flow is August to November after the monsoon; arrive at the viewpoints by 9:00 AM before afternoon mist blankets the 830-foot canyon.
destinations.practical_tip: Descend the 1,400 stone steps to the bottom of the gorge only if physically fit; carry plenty of water for the return climb.

destinations.name: Madikeri
destinations.description: Scotland of India — coffee and spice estates, ridge-top viewpoints and Kodava culture.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Fee not confirmed from a source in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Traditional Kodava spread: Akki Roti with Kadambuttu (steamed rice balls) and bamboo shoot curry (or Coorg Pandi curry), followed by fresh Coorg Arabica coffee.
destinations.best_time_tip: Visit Raja's Seat gardens at 5:30 PM to enjoy sunset views over the undulating Western Ghats valleys where Coorg kings once spent evenings.
destinations.practical_tip: Carry a light sweater or rain jacket year-round; visit Abbey Falls early morning (8:30 AM) to beat tourist bus arrivals.

destinations.name: B.R. Hills
destinations.description: Biligiri Ranganatha hills where the Eastern and Western Ghats meet — temple town, forests and safaris.
destinations.season_note: October–March; drier months are preferable for wildlife viewing.
destinations.entry_fee_note: No adult main-attraction fee confirmed; safari pricing varies.
destinations.local_dish: Traditional Soliga tribal forest honey, steaming Ragi Mudde with soppina saaru, and hot South Indian filter coffee.
destinations.best_time_tip: Best visited October to March; early morning (6:30 AM) forest safaris offer the highest likelihood of elephant, gaur, and leopard sightings.
destinations.practical_tip: The 500-year-old Biligiri Rangaswamy Temple sits on a sheer 400-meter cliff; watch for monkeys and enjoy panoramic views across the Nilgiri-Ghats ecological bridge.

destinations.name: Bandipur
destinations.description: Tiger reserve in the Nilgiri biosphere with elephant herds, dry deciduous forest and jeep safaris.
destinations.season_note: October–February; March–May can also be good for sightings.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Safari and entry prices in available listings conflict or may be outdated; omitted rather than guessed.
destinations.local_dish: South Karnataka forest meals: steamed Ragi Mudde, hot vegetable sambar, freshly cooked country beans, and spiced buttermilk.
destinations.best_time_tip: Safaris operate 6:15–9:00 AM and 3:30–6:00 PM; dawn safaris offer the coolest temperatures and highest predator activity along waterholes.
destinations.practical_tip: Wear neutral earth-toned clothing (khaki, olive, brown) on safaris and maintain absolute silence; night traffic through the national park is banned from 9:00 PM to 6:00 AM.

destinations.name: Kabini
destinations.description: River-side tiger reserve famed for boat safaris, leopards, wild dogs and dense elephant country.
destinations.season_note: Dry season roughly October–May; boat safari may be suspended in very high or low water.
destinations.entry_fee_note: Boat/jeep safari prices vary by operator and season; not confirmed in this pass.
destinations.local_dish: Jungle lodge buffet featuring Kodagu-Mysuru fusion dishes, steaming Ragi Mudde with country greens, and herbal decoction tea.
destinations.best_time_tip: Evening boat safaris along the Kabini reservoir backwaters (3:30–6:00 PM) offer world-class sightings of large Asian elephant herds congregating at the shoreline.
destinations.practical_tip: Pre-book boat and jeep safaris online well in advance through the Karnataka Forest Department or Jungle Lodges, as safari vehicle quotas are strictly limited.
